How the interview runs (sourced)

The TikTok SQL interview, as candidates report it

TikTok does not publish the format. Each row is what candidates and prep guides have described publicly, with its source; where sources disagree, the row says so. Formats change — treat every specific as reported, not official.

Roles the sources coverData Scientist and Data Engineer. We found no readable candidate report for a data-analyst loop, so this page describes none.[6][1][2]
Data science stagesRecruiter screen, a hiring-manager screen, a loop of three or four rounds of about 45 minutes each (product sense, A/B testing, SQL, machine learning) plus behavioural rounds, then a final manager conversation; all virtual.[3][4][5]
Read or debug a queryTwo candidate reports describe being given an existing query instead of a blank editor: a data scientist (June 2026) was asked to explain what a query does and what it returns, and a data engineer (September 2025) to find and fix the bug in a pre-written daily-active-users query.[1][2]
PlatformSources disagree: one 2025 guide names HackerRank for the data-science screen, another guide says SQLPad, so this page names neither.[4][5]
  1. [1] PracHub — TikTok Data Scientist: medium SQL and background follow-ups (candidate report, Jun 2026) (5 Sep 2026)
  2. [2] PracHub — TikTok Data Engineer (USDS): a final round that ended before any SQL was written (candidate report, Sep 2025) (25 Aug 2026)
  3. [3] Aced (formerly Exponent) — TikTok Data Scientist interview guide (shown as "updated 4 days ago" on 23 Nov 2026)
  4. [4] DataLemur — TikTok Data Scientist interview guide (5 Jan 2025)
  5. [5] Prepfully — TikTok Data Scientist interview process (prep guide; names no sources) (undated, read 23 Nov 2026)
  6. [6] DataLemur — TikTok SQL interview questions (practice questions; covers Data Science and Data Engineering) (5 Jan 2025)

The SQL that comes up

What TikTok SQL questions test

Named in the sources, with counts

  • Reading or debugging an existing query — 2 of the 3 candidate reports that describe the SQL
  • Window functions, such as each user's top item per day with a tie rule — both practice guides
  • Date logic: extracting a day or month and grouping by it — both practice guides

Difficulty: Not reliably reported, so this page does not grade it. The data is what the prep guides' practice questions use — videos (uploads, likes, dates), user interactions, and sign-up and confirmation events; no candidate report we could read describes the tables.

Our TikTok practice set, by skill

The 16 SQL Quest challenges tagged TikTok, resolved onto the nine Skillmap skills. A challenge exercises several skills, so shares do not sum to 100%. This is the composition of the practice set on this page, not a measurement of TikTok’s interview.

Sample questions

TikTok SQL question shapes, and where to practise them

Shapes candidates and guides report (paraphrased)

  • Given a query, explain what it does and what it returns.[1]
  • A pre-written query meant to count daily active users has a bug: find it and fix it.[2]
  • Sign-ups and text confirmations: users who did not confirm on day 1 but did on day 2.[6]
  • Videos with uploads and likes: each user's most-liked video per day, the earliest upload winning ties.[6]

Every challenge in the TikTok set, by topic

These are SQL Quest challenges matched to the topics candidates report for TikTok — not questions TikTok has asked.

Every query here runs on SQLite in your browser. Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs and window functions are written the same way in PostgreSQL, MySQL and Snowflake; dates are where they differ (SQLite's strftime('%Y-%m', ts) is to_char(ts, 'YYYY-MM') in PostgreSQL), and the app lists each difference beside every challenge.

Drill the skills the TikTok set leans on, one at a time: GROUP BY exercises · Window function practice · CTE practice · Date function practice · JOIN practice — or browse every SQL practice question.
